statement: A farmer is fencing a triangular pasture. Two of its sides measure $9$ meters and $14$ meters, and the third side is a whole number of meters. How many different lengths are possible for the third side?

choices.misconception: I found that the third side is between $5$ and $23$ and subtracted $23 - 5 = 18$, which counts one number too many.
I let the third side equal $5$ or $23$ as well, so I counted every whole number from $5$ through $23$, but those two lengths make a flat triangle.
I only used the rule that the third side is less than $9 + 14 = 23$, so I counted $1$ through $22$ and forgot it must also be more than $14 - 9 = 5$.

hints: Any two sides of a triangle must add to more than the third side.
The third side must be greater than the difference of the other two sides and less than their sum. Then count the whole numbers strictly between those values.
The third side $c$ satisfies $5 < c < 23$, so count the whole numbers $6$ through $22$.

solutions.reliable: By the triangle inequality, the third side $c$ satisfies $14 - 9 < c < 14 + 9$, so $5 < c < 23$. The whole numbers in this range are $6, 7, \ldots, 22$, and there are $22 - 6 + 1 = 17$ of them.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
